Detention of Journalist Naqaa Hamed.. An Escalation Against the Press
In a new violation of journalistic work, the Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) has demanded that the Israeli authorities immediately release Palestinian-American journalist Naqaa Hamed and publicly clarify the legal basis for her detention.  
Occupation forces abducted Naqaa — who works as a correspondent for several news outlets — at a military checkpoint near Bethlehem in the occupied West Bank. Naqaa is facing baseless espionage allegations due to her professional work, at a time when the occupation authorities have extended her detention until September 23.  
This comes as the Palestinian Prisoners’ Society warned of the dangerous escalation of arrests targeting journalists in the West Bank, which has brought the number of journalists held in Israeli prisons to 39.

A vulnerability in the system rate-limiting process for syslog message 419002 of Cisco Secure Firewall Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) Software and Cisco Secure Firewall Threat Defense (FTD) Software could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause high CPU utilization on an affected device, resulting in a denial of service (DoS) condition.
This vulnerability is due to improper rate limiting for syslog message 419002. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a flood of TCP synchronization (SYN) packets to an affected device. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause high CPU utilization, resulting in performance degradation. 

Cisco has released software updates that address this vulnerability. There are workarounds that address this vulnerability.

🌍 Russia, China veto on anti‑Iran draft will be recorded in history: Iran envoy

📌 Moscow, IRNA – Iran’s ambassador to Russia, Kazem Jalali, says that Washington has failed in its attempt to push an anti‑Iran resolution through the UN Security Council, praising Russia and China for their decisive support.

In a post on his X account late on Friday, Jalali said that the US sought to impose pressure on Iran through a new resolution, but the attempt collapsed after Russia and China opposed the draft.
​
He thanked the two countries for standing firmly by Iran and preventing an unfair and politically motivated initiative, saying their joint veto had marked a historic moment in the Council’s record.
​
He added that the threadbare instrument of sanctions belonged to a past era and had already lost its effectiveness, noting that the future world will be shaped by countries that believe in a multipolar order and multilateral cooperation.
​
The draft resolution was put to a vote at the United Nations Security Council on September 17, 2026, in New York, where the United States sought to extend the mandate of UN experts monitoring sanctions that had been reimposed on Iran under the snapback mechanism.
​
The proposal received 11 votes in favor, while Pakistan and Somalia abstained, but it ultimately failed because Russia and China vetoed the text, shutting down the effort to continue independent monitoring of the reinstated sanctions.

This year, a potential “Trump bump” ahead of the November midterms could fuel a Q4 rally. Amid ongoing turmoil—from Iran to other geopolitical setbacks—stocks and crypto might hand Trump one of his most visible and straightforward pre-election wins.
